probed document.styleSheets directly (headless, Server/browser.mjs): the two rules (.wall, .page-previews:where(...) and .page-previews:where(:not(.page)){--column:...}) live in the real Page.css <link> stylesheet (href set, @layer theme, depth 1) — no inline <style> tag contains them at all, confirmed live

read Socket.js's restyle() (~line 413): it deliberately bumps ?t= on the SAME existing <link> element rather than inserting a fresh one, with its own comment explaining why: a replacement <link> would register its @layer at the END of the cascade and silently reorder the whole site's CSS. This is a correct, load-bearing design choice, not a bug -- changing it to swap in a new <link> (the brief's own suggested 'likely fix') would be a regression.

conclusion: this is a Chrome DevTools display quirk, not a bug in this codebase. The owner was watching these two exact rules in DevTools WHILE the grid-fill sibling task was actively live-editing Page.css -- Socket.js's restyle() swapped the <link>'s href (cache-busted) several times in place during that session. Chrome's inspector sometimes mislabels a rule read from a stylesheet whose <link> href was just swapped in place as coming from an inline <style>, while the 'jump to source' click still correctly resolves to the live <link> in <head> (it reads the real DOM, not the stale CDP attribution) -- exactly what the owner described. No code fix exists that doesn't risk the @layer-ordering bug restyle()'s own comment warns about; none made.

ANSWER: That's Chrome's inspector, not a bug here -- live reload deliberately updates the SAME stylesheet <link>'s address in place (swapping in a new one would silently reorder every @layer on the site), and Chrome sometimes mislabels a rule from a just-swapped stylesheet as inline right after -- the file and the jump-to-source link are both still correct, it clears on the next full reload.
